blocks.title: Gerbes of liftings and splittings, and decomposition of the de Rham complex (general case)
blocks.html: 3. Gerbes of liftings and splittings, and decomposition of the de Rham complex (general case)
3.1. Let \(A\) be an abelian category. We will say that an object \(K\) of \(D^b(A)\) is decomposable if \(K\) is isomorphic (in \(D^b(A)\)) to a complex with zero differential.

For \(K\) to be decomposable, it is necessary and sufficient that there exist, in \(D(A)\), morphisms \(f_i : H^i K[-i] \to K\) such that \(H^i(f_i)\) is the identity map of \(H^i K\) (this condition is necessary, since it is satisfied by \(\bigoplus H^i K[-i]\), and sufficient, since the \(f_i\) induce an isomorphism \(\bigoplus H^i K[-i] \xrightarrow{\sim} K\)). If \(K\) is decomposable, one calls a decomposition of \(K\) a morphism \(f = \sum f_i : \bigoplus H^i K[-i] \to K\) such that \(H^i f\) is the identity map of \(H^i K\).

Let \(K\) be a decomposable complex such that \(K^i = 0\) for \(i \neq 0, 1\). A decomposition of \(K\) is entirely determined by the datum of \(f_1 : H^1 K[-1] \to K\) such that \(H^1 f_1\) is the identity (\(f_0\) is given by the injection \(H^0 K \hookrightarrow K^0\)). The distinguished triangle
\[ H^0 K \to K \to H^1 K[-1] \to \]
yields the exact sequence
\[ 0 \to \operatorname{Hom}(H^1 K[-1], H^0 K) \to \operatorname{Hom}(H^1 K[-1], K) \xrightarrow{a} \operatorname{Hom}(H^1 K, H^1 K), \]
which shows that the set of decompositions of \(K\) is an affine space under \(\operatorname{Hom}(H^1 K[-1], H^0 K) = \operatorname{Ext}^1(H^1 K, H^0 K)\) (inverse image under \(a\) of Id).

3.2. Let \((T, \mathcal{O})\) be a ringed site and \(K\) a complex of \(\mathcal{O}\)-modules on \(T\) with \(K^i = 0\) for \(i \neq 0, 1\). One assumes that \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\) is locally free of finite rank; the projection of \(K^1\) onto \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\) therefore admits a section locally. One assumes moreover that the projection of \(K^0\) onto \(\operatorname{Im}(d)\) also admits a section locally.

Let \(\operatorname{sc}'(K)\) be the following fibered category over \(T\): an object over \(U\) is a splitting (over \(U\)) \(s : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to K^1\) of the projection of \(K^1\) onto \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\); an arrow from \(s'\) to \(s''\) is a homomorphism \(h : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to K^0\) (over \(U\)) such that \(s'' = s' + dh\). If \(s'\) and \(s''\) are two objects over \(U\), the morphisms from \(s'\) to \(s''\) form a sheaf on \(U\): \(\operatorname{sc}'(K)\) is a prestack (in groupoids). Moreover, the hypotheses made on \(K\) imply that: a) every \(U\) admits a covering \(R\) such that the fiber category \(\operatorname{sc}'(K)(R)\) is nonempty; b) any two objects of \(\operatorname{sc}'(K)\) are locally isomorphic. The stack associated with the prestack \(\operatorname{sc}'(K)\) is therefore a gerbe (Giraud [12, III §2]), the gerbe of splittings of \(K\), denoted \(\operatorname{sc}(K)\).

For every object \(s\) of \(\operatorname{sc}(K)\), \(\mathscr{Hom}(s, s)\) is the abelian sheaf \(\mathscr{Hom}(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K)\). The gerbe \(\operatorname{sc}(K)\) admits a global object1 if and only if its class [12, IV 3.1, 3.5]
\[ \operatorname{cl} \operatorname{sc}(K) \in H^2(T, \mathscr{Hom}(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K)) = \operatorname{Ext}^2(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K) \]

is zero. If this is the case, the set of classes up to isomorphism of global objects of \(\operatorname{sc}(K)\) is an affine space under \(H^1(T, \mathscr{Hom}(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K)) = \operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K)\) (if \(s\) and \(t\) are two global objects, their "difference" \(t - s\) is the class of the torsor of local isomorphisms from \(s\) onto \(t\), cf. [12, III 2.2.6]).
Let us denote moreover by
\[ e(K) \in \operatorname{Ext}^2(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K) \]
the class defined by the degree-1 morphism of the distinguished triangle
\[ \mathscr{H}^0 K \to K \to \mathscr{H}^1 K[-1] \xrightarrow{+1}. \]

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 3.3

With the preceding notation: (a) One has

\[ \operatorname{cl} \operatorname{sc}(K) = - e(K). \]

(b) There exists a canonical affine bijection \(\alpha\), defined below, from the set of classes up to isomorphism of global objects of \(\operatorname{sc}(K)\) onto the set of decompositions of \(K\), inducing the identity on the group of translations \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K)\).

Proof▾

Let us prove (a). Choose a hypercovering \(U_{\bullet} \to T\), over \(U_0\) a section \(f : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to K^1\) of the projection of \(K^1\) onto \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\), and over \(U_1\), \(g : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to K^0\) such that \(d_1^* f - d_0^* f = dg\). Then \(h = d_2^* g - d_1^* g + d_0^* g\) is a 2-cocycle of \(U_{\bullet}\) with values in \(\mathscr{Hom}(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K)\), whose image in \(H^2(T, \mathscr{Hom}(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K))\) is \(\operatorname{cl} \operatorname{sc}(K)\) (cf. [12, IV 3.5]). On the other hand, with the sign convention of [J.-L. Verdier, Catégories dérivées, Etat 0, p. 269, in SGA 4 1/2, Springer Lecture Notes 569], \(e(K)\) is the class of the "composite" morphism

\[ \mathscr{H}^1 K[-1] \xleftarrow{\;q\;} E \xrightarrow{-\,\mathrm{pr}} \mathscr{H}^0 K[1], \]

where

\[ E = \left( \mathscr{H}^0 K \to K^0 \xrightarrow{\;d\;} K^1 \right) \]

is the cone (concentrated in degrees \(-1, 0, 1\)) of \(\mathscr{H}^0 K \to K\), \(q\) the quasi-isomorphism given by the projection of \(K^1\) onto \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\), and pr the obvious projection. Set \(M = \mathscr{H}^0 K\), \(N = \mathscr{H}^1 K\), and denote by \(\check{N}\) the dual of \(N\). The class \(e(K)\) is again the image of \(\operatorname{Id}_N \in H^0(T, \check{N} \otimes N)\) in \(H^2(T, \check{N} \otimes M) = H^2(T, \mathscr{Hom}(\mathscr{H}^1 K, \mathscr{H}^0 K))\) under the composite morphism

\[ H^0(T, \check{N} \otimes N) \xleftarrow[\simeq]{\;q\;} H^1(T, \check{N} \otimes K) \xrightarrow{-\operatorname{Id}_N \otimes \mathrm{pr}} H^2(T, \check{N} \otimes M). \]

Now

\[ c = (h, -g, f) \in \check{C}^1(U_{\bullet}, \check{N} \otimes K) = \check{C}^2(U_{\bullet}, \check{N} \otimes M) \oplus \check{C}^1(U_{\bullet}, \check{N} \otimes K^0) \oplus \check{C}^0(U_{\bullet}, \check{N} \otimes K^1) \]

is a 1-cocycle, with image \(\operatorname{Id}_N\) under \(q\), and \(-h\) under \(-\operatorname{Id}_N \otimes \mathrm{pr}\). Hence \(e(K) = -\operatorname{cl} \operatorname{sc}(K)\).

Let us now construct \(\alpha\). Let \(s\) be a global object of \(\operatorname{sc}(K)\), described by a hypercovering \(U_{\bullet} \to T\), over \(U_0\) a section \(f : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to K^1\) of the projection of \(K^1\) onto \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\), and over \(U_1\), \(h : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to K^0\) such that \(d_1^* f - d_0^* f = dh\) and \(d_2^* h - d_1^* h + d_0^* h = 0\). Then

\[ (h, f) : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to \check{\mathscr{C}}^1(U_{\bullet}, K^0) \oplus \check{\mathscr{C}}^0(U_{\bullet}, K^1) \]

is a morphism from \(\mathscr{H}^1 K[-1]\) to \(\check{\mathscr{C}}^{\bullet}(U_{\bullet}, K)\), whose image \(\alpha(s)\) in \(\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T)}(\mathscr{H}^1 K[-1], K)\) is a decomposition of \(K\). By arguments analogous to those in the proof of 2.1 (d), one checks that \(\alpha(s)\) is independent of the choices of \((U_{\bullet}, f, h)\), and depends only on the class of \(s\) up to isomorphism. It remains to check that, if \(t\) is a second global object, one has \(\alpha(t) - \alpha(s) = t - s\). With the notation above, one then has

\[ (k, g) - (h, f) = v + d u : \mathscr{H}^1 K \to \check{\mathscr{C}}^1(U_{\bullet}, K), \]

where \(u\) is here regarded as an arrow from \(\mathscr{H}^1 K\) to \(\check{\mathscr{C}}^0(U_{\bullet}, K)\) and \(d\) denotes the total differential of the complex \(\check{\mathscr{C}}(U_{\bullet}, K)\). One thus indeed has \(\alpha(t) - \alpha(s) = t - s\), which completes the proof of (b).

3.4. Let \(S\) be a scheme of characteristic \(p > 0\), \(X\) a smooth scheme over \(S\), and \(F : X \to X'\) the relative Frobenius (1.1). Suppose we are given a scheme \(\tilde{S}\), flat over \(\mathbf{Z}/p^2\), whose reduction modulo \(p\) is \(S\). We propose to describe the gerbe of splittings of \(K = \tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) in terms of liftings of \(X'\) over \(\tilde{S}\).

For every scheme \(Y\) smooth over \(S\), the gerbe of liftings of \(Y\) over \(\tilde{S}\), denoted \(\operatorname{Rel}(Y, \tilde{S})\), is the gerbe on \(Y\) having as objects over an open set \(U\) the schemes \(\tilde{U}\) flat over \(\tilde{S}\) having \(U\) as reduction modulo \(p\) (i.e. equipped with an isomorphism of their reduction modulo \(p\) with \(U\)). A morphism \(\tilde{U}' \to \tilde{U}''\) is a morphism of \(\tilde{S}\)-schemes whose reduction modulo \(p\) is the identity. The sheaf of automorphisms of any lifting of \(U\) is the abelian sheaf \(\Theta_{U/S} = \mathscr{Hom}(\Omega^1_{U/S}, \mathcal{O}_U)\) of relative vector fields on \(U\).

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 3.5

There exists a canonical equivalence of gerbes, defined below,

\[ \Phi : \operatorname{Rel}(X', \tilde{S}) \to \operatorname{sc}(\tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}), \]

inducing the identity on the sheaves of automorphisms of the objects.
(Note that, for the two gerbes considered, the sheaf of automorphisms of an object is the sheaf \(\Theta_{X'/S}\) of relative vector fields.)
Taking 3.3 into account, one deduces:

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 3.6

(a) For \(X'\) to admit a lifting over \(\tilde{S}\), it is necessary and sufficient that \(\tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) be decomposable.

(b) If this is the case, \(\alpha \circ \Phi\) is an affine bijection from the set of classes up to isomorphism of liftings of \(X'\) over \(\tilde{S}\) onto the set of decompositions of \(\tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\), inducing the identity on the group of translations \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathscr{H}^1 F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}, \mathscr{H}^0 F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S})\) (isomorphic, by Cartier, to \(\operatorname{Ext}^1(\Omega^1_{X'/S}, \mathcal{O}_{X'}) = H^1(X', \Theta)\)).
The arguments of 2.1 (a) and of the proof of 2.3 also give:

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 3.7

(a) With every lifting of \(X'\) over \(\tilde{S}\) there is canonically associated an isomorphism of \(D(X')\)

\[ \bigoplus_{i < p} \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \xrightarrow{\sim} \tau_{< p} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \]

inducing \(C^{-1}\) on \(\mathscr{H}^{\bullet}\).

(b) If \(X\) has relative dimension \(\leqslant p\), if \(X'\) lifts over \(\tilde{S}\), and if \(H^{p+1}(X', \Omega^p_{X'/S}) = 0\) (which is the case for example if \(S\) is affine and \(X\) proper over \(S\)), then \(F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) is decomposable, i.e. there exists an isomorphism of \(D(X')\)

\[ \bigoplus_i \Omega^i_{X'/S}[-i] \xrightarrow{\sim} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S} \]

inducing \(C^{-1}\) on \(\mathscr{H}^{\bullet}\).

Proof of 3.5▾

Let \(U\) be an open set of \(X\) and \(\tilde{U}'\) a lifting of \(U'\). The task is to attach (functorially) to \(\tilde{U}'\) an object of \(\operatorname{sc}(\tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S})\) over \(U\). It suffices to construct this object depending on an auxiliary choice, together with a transitive system of isomorphisms between the objects attached to the various choices; it even suffices to carry out this construction locally, provided one has compatibility with the gluing. The auxiliary choice is that of a lifting \(\tilde{U}\) of \(U\) over \(\tilde{S}\) and of a lifting \(\tilde{F} : \tilde{U} \to \tilde{U}'\) of \(F\). Such liftings exist locally. To \((\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\) one attaches the following splitting \(s(\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\):

(cf. 2.1 (b)): since \(F^* : \Omega^1_{U'/S} \to F_* \Omega^1_{U/S}\) is zero, the image of \(\tilde{F}^* : \Omega^1_{\tilde{U}'/\tilde{S}} \to F_* \Omega^1_{\tilde{U}/\tilde{S}}\) is contained in \(p F_* \Omega^1_{\tilde{U}/\tilde{S}}\); one defines \(s(\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\) by étale localization and reduction to the case where \(U\) is the standard affine space \(\mathbf{A}^n_S = S[t_1, \ldots, t_n]\), \(\tilde{U}'\) the canonical lifting \(\mathbf{A}^n_{\tilde{S}}\) of \(U'\), \(\tilde{F}\) given by \(t_i \mapsto t_i^p\), that \(p^{-1} \tilde{F}^*\) lifts the Cartier isomorphism \(C^{-1} : \Omega^1_{U'/S} \to \mathscr{H}^1 F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{U/S}\), hence that \(s(\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\) is indeed a splitting of \(\tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\).

For given \(\tilde{U}\), the liftings \(\tilde{F}\) of \(F\) form an affine space under \(H^0(U, F^* \Theta_{U'/S})\) and each \(D \in H^0(U, F^* \Theta_{U'/S})\) defines \(H(D) : \Omega^1_{U'/S} \to F_* \mathcal{O}_U\). From the fact that \(dF = 0\) it follows that, for every automorphism \(a\) of the lifting \(\tilde{U}\), one has \(\tilde{F} \circ a = \tilde{F}\).

Let us construct a transitive system of isomorphisms between the \(s(\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\). Consider two choices \((\tilde{U}_i, \tilde{F}_i)\) (\(i = 1, 2\)). Locally, the liftings \(\tilde{U}_1\) and \(\tilde{U}_2\) of \(U\) are isomorphic. Let us choose locally an isomorphism \(u : \tilde{U}_1 \to \tilde{U}_2\). The lifting \(\tilde{F}_2 \cdot u\) of \(F\) does not depend on the choice of \(u\); it therefore comes from a lifting of \(F\) again denoted \(\tilde{F}_2 \cdot u : \tilde{U}_1 \to \tilde{U}'_2\). One has \(s(\tilde{U}_2, \tilde{F}_2) = s(\tilde{U}_1, \tilde{F}_2 \cdot u)\). On the other hand, if \(D\) is the difference between \(\tilde{F}_1\) and \(\tilde{F}_2 \cdot u\) (\(u : \tilde{U}_1 \to \tilde{U}_2\), \(= pD\)), one checks that

\[ s(\tilde{U}_2, \tilde{F}_2) - s(\tilde{U}_1, \tilde{F}_1) = dH(D). \]

One takes \(H(D)\) as the isomorphism from \(s(\tilde{U}_1, \tilde{F}_1)\) onto \(s(\tilde{U}_2, \tilde{F}_2)\). This is the desired transitive system of isomorphisms, and \(\Phi(\tilde{U}')\) is the "common value" of the \(s(\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\).

If \(v : \tilde{U}'_1 \to \tilde{U}'_2\) is an isomorphism of liftings of \(U'\), each auxiliary choice \((\tilde{U}, \tilde{F})\) for \(\tilde{U}'_1\) defines one, \((\tilde{U}, v \circ \tilde{F})\) for \(\tilde{U}'_2\). One defines \(\Phi(v)\) by the commutative diagram

\[ \xymatrix{ s(\tilde{U}, \tilde{F}) \ar@{=}[r] \ar[d]^{\simeq} & s(\tilde{U}, v \circ \tilde{F}) \ar[d]^{\simeq} \\ \Phi(U'_1) \ar[r]^{\Phi(v)} & \Phi(U'_2). } \]

In particular, for \(\tilde{U}'_1 = \tilde{U}'_2\), \(\Phi(v)\) is the composite of \(F : \mathcal{O}_{U'} \to F_* \mathcal{O}_U\) and of the difference \(v - \operatorname{Id} : \Omega^1_{U'} \to \mathcal{O}_{U'}\).

It is clear that \(\Phi\) is a morphism of gerbes, inducing the identity on the sheaves of automorphisms of the objects; it is an equivalence.

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 3.8

The homomorphism \(\varphi_S^1 : \Omega^1_{X'/S}[-1] \to F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S}\) of 2.1 (or of its variant 2.2 (i)) in fact depends only on \(\tilde{S}\): with the notation of 3.3 and 3.5, one has

\[ \varphi_S^1 = \alpha \circ \Phi(\tilde{X}'). \]

If \(\tilde{X}_1, \tilde{X}_2\) are two liftings of \(X\), \(\varphi_{X_2}^1 - \varphi_{X_1}^1\) is therefore the class, in \(H^1(X', \Theta_{X'/S})\), of the difference \((\tilde{X}'_2 - \tilde{X}'_1)\).

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 3.9

Let \(\tilde{S}\) be a lifting of \(S\) over \(\mathbf{Z}/p^2\). By 3.5, the gerbe \(\operatorname{Rel}(X', \tilde{S})\) is independent of \(S\): it is \(\operatorname{sc}(\tau_{\leqslant 1} F_* \Omega^{\bullet}_{X/S})\). Let us show how to check this independence directly. Let \(\tilde{S}_1\) and \(\tilde{S}_2\) be two liftings of \(S\) and \(T = \tilde{S}_1 \coprod_S \tilde{S}_2\) their amalgamated sum. The structure sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{S}_i}\) is an extension of \(\mathcal{O}_S\) by \(\mathcal{O}_S\): \(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{S}_i}\) admits a two-step filtration, whose successive quotients \(I_i\) and \(\mathcal{O}_S\) are an extension of \(\mathcal{O}_S\) by \(I_i \oplus \mathcal{O}_S\), with again \((I_1 \oplus I_2)^2 = 0\). Multiplication by \(p\) on \(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{S}_i}\) (resp. \(\mathcal{O}_T\)) factors through an isomorphism of \(\mathcal{O}_S\)-modules \(\mathcal{O}_S \xrightarrow{\sim} I_i\) (resp. \(\mathcal{O}_S \xrightarrow{\sim} I_1 \oplus I_2\)) via the diagonal map \(\mathcal{O}_S \to I_1 \oplus I_2\). Let \(\bar{T}\) be the reduction modulo \(p\) of \(T\). The structure sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_T\) being an extension of \(\mathcal{O}_S\) by an ideal of square zero, the Frobenius of \(\bar{T}\) factors through \(S\): one has a commutative diagram

\[ \xymatrix{ \tilde{S}_i \ar[d] & S \ar@{_{(}->}[l] \ar[r] \ar[d] & S \ar[d] \\ T \ar@{_{(}->}[r] & \bar{T} \ar[ur]^{f} \ar[r]_{F_{\bar{T}}} & \bar{T} } \]

and therefore, in particular, a lifting \(f^* X\) of \(X' = F_S^* X\) over \(\bar{T}\). For \(i = 1, 2\), the amalgamated sum \(T\) is again the amalgamated sum, over \(S\), of \(\bar{T}\) and \(\tilde{S}_i\). The functor "inverse image over \(\tilde{S}_i\)" is therefore an equivalence from the gerbe of liftings of \(f^* X\) over \(T\) to that of liftings of \(X'\) over \(\tilde{S}_i\). Composing these equivalences (\(i = 1, 2\)), one obtains an equivalence \(\operatorname{Rel}(X', \tilde{S}_1) \xrightarrow{\sim} \operatorname{Rel}(X', \tilde{S}_2)\).

footnotes.html: See 3.3 (b) for a description of the global objects.
